ticket.title: Review outfeed gate - should it run the configured chain, and should --tier make the verification matrix executable
ticket.description:
Review what `outfeed gate` is for, and whether it should execute the configured chain by tier.

WHAT IT DOES TODAY (measured): outfeed-core has a hard-coded step matrix - gate_steps() returns fmt, clippy and their siblings as GateStep values - and run_gate_steps(dir, steps, skip, reporter) runs them with a progress reporter and a --skip list. So it is a real gate runner already, repository-scoped, with no receipt.

TWO PROBLEMS, both documentation-adjacent and one structural:
  1. `outfeed gate --help` says "Verify every member repository tracks a fresh Cargo.lock". That is not what it runs. Same disease as miter audit, whose help described a report while thirteen chains gated on its exit code (ADR 0011).
  2. There are two descriptions of what must pass in a repository: gate_steps() in outfeed-core, and the per-repository strings in [storypole] verification_commands. They can drift, and nothing compares them.

THE PROPOSAL WORTH ASSESSING: `outfeed gate --tier N`, where N selects a row of the verification matrix in AGENTS.md section 4. That matrix is currently PROSE ONLY - Tier 1 inner loop (cargo check, targeted nextest), Tier 2 atomic commit (fmt check, clippy, nextest, miter audit, chalkline docs check), Tier 3 task completion (workspace-wide), Tier 4 release (contracts, lockfiles, docs, full suite). Every agent and every chain re-types those command lists by hand, which is where a wrong flag comes from - this session alone typed the Tier 2 list dozens of times and lost a cycle each time to `cargo fmt --all` versus `cargo fmt --check`.

VALUE: yes, if it makes the law executable rather than duplicated. A tier flag turns a paragraph nobody can verify into a command, and gives the suite one place to fix a step.

RISK TO DESIGN AROUND: a second runner. storypole verify is ticket-scoped and writes a receipt naming repository, branch and commit window; outfeed gate is repository-scoped and writes nothing. Two runners with different semantics is how GB-79 diverged. So the decision this ticket must make first is which one OWNS the chain definition - probably: outfeed gate executes the configured chain, gate_steps() becomes the default when a repository configures none, and storypole verify calls the same definition and adds the receipt.

ACCEPTANCE (proposed): `outfeed gate --tier 2` runs exactly the Tier 2 row and names each step as it runs; `--tier` and `--skip` compose; a repository with a configured chain gets that chain, not the hard-coded default; the help text states what runs and whether it writes anything; and a test asserts the Tier 2 row matches AGENTS.md section 4, so the law and the tool cannot drift.
